page: Microsoft Azure E16a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the EAv4 family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7452 processor featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 410 GB SSD.

Benchmark data indicates that the server delivers average multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by its stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory read bandwidth for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also falls within the average range. However, the server exhibits poor single-core CPU performance, placing in the bottom 10% for stress-ng single-core tests. Additionally, large block uncached memory write bandwidth is weak, and medium-sized LLM inference speeds are limited.

Given its high memory density and bundled local SSD storage, the E16a_v4 offers a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring substantial memory without requiring top-tier single-threaded compute performance. It is well-suited for relational database hosting, caching layers such as Redis, static web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E16a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EAv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 410 GB of local SSD storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this x86_64 server delivers average multi-core CPU performance, memory read bandwidth, and database operation speeds, though its single-core performance and uncached memory write speeds are relatively weak. With an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the E16a_v4 provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads. It is highly suitable for database hosting, caching layers, and general-purpose memory-heavy enterprise applications.
